title: Starting sounds
goal: Twenty-two consonant sounds start a syllable. Seven are one key; the rest are neighbours pressed together.

blocks.x: Say the sound, strike the letter.
The rest are built from keys that sit next to each other. `P`+`W` is *b*, `T`+`K` is *d*, `P`+`H` is *m*.

blocks.x: Strike any of these and watch the board label.
Three starts are chosen by the spelling, not the sound, so words that sound alike can differ: `wh` is [[WH]] (*when*), `wr` is [[WR]] (*write*), and `sc` as in *scan* is [[SK]]. Lesson 9 shows why.
No sound is left off. If a word begins with a sound, its key is there; the dictionary may drop a sound only in a brief you memorise, never by accident.
